sharing.title: Session sharing
sharing.start_desc: You make a code and send it to them.
sharing.join_desc: You paste the code they sent you.
sharing.read_write_warn: They will be able to type into your terminal as you. Enforced on this machine; you can switch it back at any time.
sharing.preparing: Finding a route… this takes a few seconds.
sharing.waiting: Waiting for them to connect. This closes on its own once they do.
sharing.fail_no_path: No route between the two machines. This is almost always a NAT that blocks direct connections. It works if both of you are on the same network or VPN, or with a TURN server added under Settings → Sharing.
sharing.fail_bad_code: That code is not for this share. Check it was copied completely.
sharing.fail_tampered: A message arrived that could not be verified, so the connection was closed.
sharing.fail_timeout: The other side did not connect in time.
sharing.remote_view_only: View only. They have not allowed typing.
sharing.enable_desc: Share a terminal with another person, peer to peer, encrypted end to end. Off by default. While it is off none of this code is loaded, and while it is on nothing connects until you click Share.
sharing.ice_desc: Used only when you click Share, and only to find a route to the other machine. Your list, in your order.
sharing.ice_empty: No servers. Sharing will work only on the same network.
sharing.stun_note: STUN only answers "what is my public address?". It carries none of your traffic, costs nothing to run, and the defaults are public servers run by Google and Cloudflare.
sharing.turn_note: TURN relays your traffic when a direct route cannot be found. There is no free public TURN worth trusting, so none is included. If you run one, or your team does, add it here.
recipes.none_yet: No recipes yet. Create one, or browse the registry.

recipes.risk_none: Nothing risky found. That is not the same as safe.
recipes.understated: The author declared this {{declared}}, but it looks {{actual}}.
recipes.declared_above_scan: Rated {{declared}} by its author. The scan alone found nothing worse; it cannot see through variables.
recipes.opaque: Line {{lines}} downloads and runs code. Nothing here can see what arrives.

mcp.confirm_title: An AI wants to run this
mcp.mode_desc: How much you want to be asked. Guards still apply in every mode — a mode only decides whether a human is asked.
mcp.mode_moot: The current agent cannot type, so the mode makes no difference.
mcp.mode_dangerous_hint: Run everything without asking, including commands that destroy data.
mcp.mode_dangerous_active: Dangerous mode is on. Commands run without asking, including ones that destroy data.
mcp.mode_dangerous_confirm: Dangerous mode lets an AI wipe disks, drop databases and take hosts down with no confirmation. Enable it?
mcp.shared_desc: What an AI can read right now. Turn sharing off on a terminal tab, or stop it here.
mcp.shared_none: Nothing is shared. The server is listening, but no session is exposed.
mcp.regenerate_confirm: Replacing the token immediately locks out every client configured with the old one. You will need to re-add the server everywhere. Continue?
mcp.token_regenerated: Token replaced. Every client using the old one is now locked out.
mcp.port_locked: Stop the server to change the port
mcp.mode_ask_hint: Confirm every command before it runs.
mcp.mode_auto_safe_hint: Run read-only commands without asking. Anything that changes the system still asks.
mcp.mode_auto_hint: Run everything without asking, except destructive commands.
mcp.share_tab: Share this session with the AI
mcp.enable_desc: Let an AI client read and type into sessions you share. Off by default; nothing listens until you turn it on.
mcp.port_desc: 0 lets the system pick a free port.
mcp.token_hint: Stored encrypted in your vault and reused across restarts, so a client configured once keeps working. Regenerate to lock out anything using the old one.
mcp.listening_nothing_shared: Listening. No session is shared yet — turn sharing on for a terminal tab.
mcp.agent_desc: The agent decides which tools the AI gets, not just how it behaves. A read-only agent has no way to type.
mcp.connect_desc: Pick your tool and paste this. Every client spells it differently.
mcp.unverified: This syntax is not in the vendor's own documentation — check it connects.
mcp.confirm_notice: Nothing runs unless you approve it. Closing this window rejects the command.

tofu.encryption_desc: Encrypts the state file and saved plans with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from this passphrase (PBKDF2). The passphrase stays in Reach's vault and reaches OpenTofu as an environment variable; the generated HCL only names the variable. An OpenTofu feature (1.7+); Terraform cannot read the result.
tofu.encryption_warning: Lose the passphrase and the state cannot be read by anyone, Reach included. Keep a copy somewhere you trust.
